building.local_amendments_note: Summit County's own Building Code (Codified Ordinances Part Thirteen) is administrative: permits, fees, inspections, contractor registration, demolition, unsafe buildings, flood damage. fixtures.basis: Summit County, which enforces the building code in Akron, incorporates 'the current State of Ohio adopted version' of the Ohio Building Code and Ohio Plumbing Code by reference and its own Part Thirteen has no toilet, fixture or restroom provision (full text searched). State law (ORC 3781.01, state pack) allows local rules only where they don't conflict with the Board of Building Standards' rules. Akron's Title 19 could not be opened, so for the city's own code this is 'none found'. The state pack's counts stand.

permit.exempt_list_quote: 102.10 Work exempt from approval. Approval is not required for the following work; however, this work is still to comply with all applicable provisions of the rules of the board: Building: 1. One-story detached accessory structures used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses and similar uses, provided the floor area does not exceed one hundred twenty square feet (11.15 m2) and playground structures. 2. Fences not over seven feet (1829 mm) high. 3. Retaining walls which are not over four feet (1219 mm) in height measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, unless supporting a surcharge or impounding Class I, II or III-A liquids. 4. Water tanks supported directly upon grade if the capacity does not exceed five thousand gallons (18 927 L) and the ratio of height to diameter or width does not exceed two to one. 5. Sidewalks, parking lots and driveways not more than thirty inches (762 mm) above grade and not over any basement or story below and which are not part of an accessible route. 6. Finishes not regulated by this code, decorating, or other work defined as maintenance or minor repair. 7. Temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets and scenery. 8. Window awnings supported by an exterior wall of Group R-3. [items 9 to 18: temporary structures and tents, storage tanks, battery smoke alarms, crypts, signs, emergency occupancy] [...] 102.10.2 Minor repairs. Minor repairs to structures may be made without application or notice to the building official. Such repairs are not to include the cutting away of any wall, partition or portion thereof, the removal or cutting of any structural beam or load bearing support, or the removal or change of any required means of egress, or rearrangement of parts of a structure affecting the egress requirements; nor do minor repairs include addition to, alteration of, replacement or relocation of any standpipe, water supply, sewer, drainage, drain leader, gas, soil, waste, vent or similar piping, electric wiring or mechanical or other work affecting public health or general safety.
permit.note: Summit County's Building Code requires a permit for all work 'subject to the exceptions stated in the OBC', so the exempt list in Akron is Ohio's (rule 4101:1-1-01, Section 102.10, reread today). Toilet partitions or compartments are not named. Item 6 exempts 'finishes not regulated by this code', while the state pack shows the code regulates toilet partitions as interior finish (fire test for HDPE), so the list doesn't settle it. 'Partition' in 102.10.2 means a wall. The county's FAQ answers the permit question only for sheds and fences; Akron's FAQ only for retaining walls, fences, basements, driveways and sidewalks.
permit.second_quote: 1305.01 REQUIREMENT. (a) No building or structure shall be constructed, altered, removed or demolished nor shall the occupancy be changed from one use or use group to another; nor shall any equipment or fixtures be installed or altered if installation of such equipment or fixture is regulated by this Building Code, without first filing an application with the Building Official and obtaining a permit therefor. [...] 1305.02 EXCEPTIONS. (a) A permit, as required by Section 1305.01, shall be required for all work, subject to the exceptions stated in the OBC and the RCO.
permit.required_quote: 105.1 Approvals required. Any owner or owner's representative who intends to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, or change the occupancy of a building or structure, or portion thereof [...] is to first make application to the building official and obtain the required approval.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Akron job sites. Price your restroom, choose a material and see the Ohio rules Summit County enforces.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Akron offices, hospitals, university buildings and manufacturing plants, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Ohio's statewide building rules set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building, and Summit County enforces them in Akron. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** building permits for Akron come from the Summit County Department of Building Standards, and the City of Akron reviews the same project separately before the county can issue one. The county requires a permit for alterations unless the work is on Ohio's exempt list. That list covers decorating, maintenance, minor repairs and finishes the building rules don't regulate, and doesn't name toilet partitions. Ask Summit County Building Standards at (330) 630-7280 whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the Summit County Department of Building Standards
page.install_rule: Akron requires contractors in every trade to register with the City when the work they do needs a permit, with an Akron tax registration number, $3 million of liability insurance and workers' compensation cover. Summit County Building Standards, which issues Akron's building permits, no longer registers contractors and asks for a certificate of insurance and a federal tax ID with each permit application. Ohio licenses only five commercial trades at state level: electrical, HVAC, hydronics, plumbing and refrigeration. Partition installation isn't one of them. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor whose work needs a permit in Akron registers with the City first.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on state, county and city projects over $250,000 for new construction or $75,000 for remodeling, Ohio law requires at least the wage the state sets for each trade in each county; school district projects are exempt from that law. The state publishes its Summit County rates on a portal that needs a login. On federally funded building work in Summit County, the federal rate for a carpenter is $36.29 an hour plus $23.79 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 6.75% in Akron: 5.75% state, 0.5% Summit County and 0.5% transit authority.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals and medical offices:** phenolic or stainless steel that stands up to frequent disinfecting, with full-height privacy stalls in public areas.

page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; Ohio Building Code (OAC 4101:1, 2021 International Building Code with Ohio amendments, effective March 1, 2024, amended October 15, 2025; named by Summit County as the 2024 Ohio Building Code), Chapter 11 with ICC A117.1-2017 (new construction and additions) and ICC A117.1-2009 (alterations), Section 102.10 for work exempt from approval; Ohio Plumbing Code (OAC 4101:3, 2021 International Plumbing Code with Ohio amendments); Codified Ordinances of Summit County, Part Thirteen (County of Summit Building Code, amended by Ordinance 2024-047, effective March 5, 2024) for permits; Akron Code of Ordinances Title 19 (Building Code); NFPA 286 for HDPE.
